parsed.explanation: The quote is verbatim and carries no hidden finite-ground-set hypothesis (the lemma explicitly allows an infinite set P, and the application is to P(a_i) over all primes). The counterexample checks out: E_i = {a_1,...,a_i,b_i} is pairwise intersecting (all contain a_1) and E_1 has size 2. For each k>=2, T_k = {b_1,...,b_{k-1},a_k} meets every E_i (b_i meets E_i for i<k; a_k meets E_i for i>=k) and every element is essential (dropping b_i loses E_i, dropping a_k loses E_k), so the T_k together with {a_1} are infinitely many inclusion-minimal finite transversals. The finite-blocker fact is false; the tree/König argument must fail. Moreover the lemma itself fails on this family: each B_j must be a transversal, and each T_k must contain some B_j, forcing B_j = T_k, so no finite list exists. Since the write-up derives finiteness of b_1,...,b_s solely from pairwise intersection and never bounds the primes occurring (no large-prime erasure argument), the construction of S, L and T collapses; the proof is invalid as written.
